$comment: The manifest seeds 1.46.2 - the LAST version already released under these coordinates, which is
what release-please reads it as. It is not the version to release next. The cutover commit is a
`feat!:`, so the first release cut here is 2.0.0: derived, not declared. Asserting 2.0.0 in the
manifest instead told release-please 2.0.0 was already out and to propose the NEXT one.
Re-basing had to go UP. 1.46.2 is on Central already, built from the compose-ai-tools tree these
modules were extracted from; restarting at 1.0.0 would rank below it and make `latest` resolve
to the stale upstream artifact. See docs/VERSIONING.md.
last-release-sha is that 1.46.2 release commit, the parent of the extraction. Without it
release-please walks all 709 inherited upstream commits and writes their history into this
Versions here are INDEPENDENT of compose-ai-tools. That repository consumes these coordinates
at the version its gradle/libs.versions.toml pins; it no longer builds these modules.
